messages.command.arch.description:
Print machine architecture.

Print machine hardware name.

Note: This implementation displays the Windows processor architecture.
messages.command.b2sum.description:

With no FILE, or when FILE is -, read standard input.

Uses WinuxCmd's portable BLAKE2b implementation, matching GNU b2sum's default 512-bit digest and --length truncation behavior.

messages.command.b2sum.option.ignore-missing: don't fail or report status for missing files
messages.command.b2sum.option.length: digest length in bits; must be multiple of 8
messages.command.b2sum.option.quiet: don't print OK for each successfully verified file
messages.command.b2sum.option.status: don't output anything, status code shows success
messages.command.b2sum.option.strict: with --check, exit non-zero for any invalid input
messages.command.b2sum.option.warn: warn about improperly formatted checksum lines
messages.command.b2sum.option.zero: end each output line with NUL, not newline
messages.command.base32.description:
Base32 encode or decode FILE, or standard input, to standard output.
With no FILE, or when FILE is -, read standard input.
The input may contain newlines when decoding. Use --ignore-garbage to
attempt to recover from any other non-alphabet bytes.
messages.command.base32.option.wrap: wrap encoded lines after COLS character (default 76). Use 0 to disable line wrapping
messages.command.base64.description:
Encode or decode FILE, or standard input, to standard output.
With no FILE, or when FILE is -, read standard input.

The data are encoded as described for the base64 alphabet in RFC
4648. When decoding, the input may contain newlines in addition
to the bytes of the formal base64 alphabet. Use --ignore-garbage
to attempt to recover from any other non-alphabet bytes in the
encoded stream.
messages.command.base64.option.wrap: wrap encoded lines after COLS character (default 76). Use 0 to disable line wrapping
messages.command.basename.description:
Print NAME with any leading directory components removed.
If specified, also remove a trailing SUFFIX.
messages.command.basename.option.multiple: support multiple arguments and treat each as a NAME
messages.command.basename.option.zero: end each output line with NUL, not newline
messages.command.basenc.description:
Encode or decode FILE, or standard input, using the selected encoding.
With no FILE, or when FILE is -, read standard input. ENCODING is one of
--base64, --base64url, --base32, --base32hex, --base16, --base2lsbf,
--base2msbf, --base58, or --z85.
messages.command.basenc.option.base2lsbf: bit string, least significant bit first
messages.command.basenc.option.base2msbf: bit string, most significant bit first
messages.command.basenc.option.wrap: wrap encoded lines after COLS character (default 76). Use 0 to disable line wrapping
messages.command.cal.description:
Display a calendar.
Display a calendar for the specified month or year. If no arguments are given, display the current month.
messages.command.cat.description:
Concatenate FILE(s) to standard output.
With no FILE, or when FILE is -, read standard input.

Examples:
  cat f g  Output f's contents, then g's contents.
  cat      Copy standard input to standard output.
messages.command.cat.synopsis: concatenate files and print on the standard output
messages.command.chattr.description:
Change Windows file attributes.
Supported flags are R,H,S,A,I,T,O for readonly, hidden, system, archive, not indexed, temporary, and offline.
[DIFFERS] Attribute flags differ from GNU chattr (Linux ext4).
messages.command.chcon.description:
Change the SELinux security context of each FILE.

WinuxCmd accepts the GNU-compatible command line surface for chcon, but
Windows does not provide SELinux file contexts. This command therefore

supported on Windows.

chcon [OPTION]... CONTEXT FILE...

messages.command.chgrp.description:
Change the group of each FILE to GROUP.

Mandatory arguments to long options are mandatory for short options too.

  -c, --changes          like verbose but report only when a change is made
  -f, --silent           suppress most error messages
  -f, --quiet            suppress most error messages
  -v, --verbose          output a diagnostic for every file processed
  -R, --recursive        operate on files and directories recursively
  -h, --no-dereference   affect symbolic links instead of any referenced file
      --dereference      affect the referent of each symbolic link (default)
  -H                     command line symbolic links are followed
  -L                     indirect symbolic links are followed
  -P                     no symbolic links are followed (default)

messages.command.chgrp.option.changes: like verbose but report only when a change is made
messages.command.chgrp.option.dereference: affect the referent of each symbolic link (default)
messages.command.chgrp.option.from: change only if current group is GROUP
messages.command.chgrp.option.no-dereference: affect symbolic links instead of any referenced file
messages.command.chgrp.option.recursive: operate on files and directories recursively
messages.command.chgrp.option.reference: use RFILE's group instead of specifying GROUP
messages.command.chgrp.option.verbose: output a diagnostic for every file processed
messages.command.chmod.description:
Change the mode of each FILE to MODE.

Each MODE is of the form '[ugoa]*([-+=]([rwxXst]*|[ugo]))+'.

  -L  traverse every symlink to a directory
  -P  do not traverse any symbolic links (default)

file attributes. Write permission is mapped to the read-only attribute.

messages.command.chmod.option.changes: like verbose but report only when a change is made

messages.command.chown.description:
Change the owner and/or group of each FILE.

messages.command.chown.option.verbose: output a diagnostic for every file processed
messages.command.chroot.description:
Run COMMAND with root directory set to NEWROOT.

WinuxCmd accepts the GNU-compatible command line surface for chroot, but
Windows does not provide a safe equivalent to POSIX chroot semantics.
This command therefore acts as a compatibility placeholder and reports
that changing the root directory is not supported on Windows.
messages.command.chroot.option.skip-chdir: do not change working directory to '/'
messages.command.cksum.description:
Print CRC (default), SYSV, or BSD checksum and byte counts of each FILE.

With no FILE, or when FILE is -, read standard input.

  -c, --check           read and verify checksums from FILE

      --tag             create a BSD-style checksum

messages.command.clear.description:
Clear the terminal screen.

Clears the terminal screen by sending ANSI escape sequences.
This works on Windows Terminal, modern terminals, and terminals that support ANSI escape codes.
messages.command.cmp.description:
Compare two files byte by byte.

Compare FILE1 with FILE2.

messages.command.col.description:

  -b    do not output backspaces

  -p    pass unknown control sequences
  -x    output spaces instead of tabs
  -l    buffer at least NUM lines (default 128)

messages.command.date.description:
Display the current time in the given FORMAT, or set the system date.

FORMAT controls the output. Interpreted sequences are:
  %Y   Year (4 digits)
  %y   Year (2 digits)
  %m   Month (01-12)
  %d   Day (01-31)
  %H   Hour (00-23)
  %I   Hour (01-12)
  %M   Minute (00-59)
  %S   Second (00-60)
  %F   Full date; same as %Y-%m-%d
  %T   Time; same as %H:%M:%S
  %z   Numeric time zone offset
  %p   AM/PM
  %a   Abbreviated weekday name
  %A   Full weekday name
  %b   Abbreviated month name
  %B   Full month name

messages.command.dir.description:
List information about files (the current directory by default).
dir is equivalent to ls -C; it lists files in columns.

Mandatory arguments to long options are mandatory for short options too.

  -a, --all                  do not ignore entries starting with .
  -A, --almost-all           do not list implied . and ..
  -b, --escape               print C-style escapes for nongraphic characters
  -B, --ignore-backups       do not list implied entries ending with ~
  -C                         list entries by columns (default)
  -d, --directory            list directories themselves, not their contents
  -F, --classify             append indicator (one of */=>@|) to entries
  -g                         like -l, but do not list owner
  -h, --human-readable       with -l and -s, print sizes like 1K 234M 2G
  -i, --inode                print the index number of each file
  -l                         use a long listing format
  -m                         fill width with a comma separated list of entries

  -s, --size                 print the allocated size of each file, in blocks

  -u                         with -lt: sort by, and show, access time
  -U                         do not sort; list entries in directory order
  -v                         natural sort of (version) numbers within text
  -w, --width=COLS           assume screen is COLS wide
  -x                         list entries by lines across
  -X                         sort alphabetically by entry extension
  -1                         list one file per line

dir is a wrapper around ls with -C (columns) as the default format.

print the resolved absolute path of the current directory.

All components of the path must exist (no symlinks are followed).
The last component may be non-existent.

Options:
  -E, --canonicalize           all but the last component must exist
  -m, --canonicalize-missing   no path components need to exist
  -e, --canonicalize-existing   all components must exist
  -L, --logical                 resolve '..' before symlinks (accepted)
  -P, --physical                resolve symlinks before '..' (accepted)
  -q, --quiet                   suppress most error messages
  -s, --strip, --no-symlinks    do not expand symlinks
      --relative-to=DIR         print the resolved path relative to DIR
      --relative-base=DIR       print relative paths below DIR
  -z, --zero                    end output with NUL instead of newline

messages.command.realpath.option.canonicalize-mis: no path components need to exist
messages.command.realpath.option.relative-to: print the resolved path relative to DIR
messages.command.realpath.option.zero: end output with NUL byte instead of newline

that are at least MIN characters long. With no FILE, read standard input.

Mandatory arguments to long options are mandatory for short options too.

  -a, --all                scan each file in its entirety (default)
  -n, --bytes=MIN          print sequences of at least MIN characters (default 4)
  -t, --radix=RADIX        print offset before each string: o=octal, d=decimal, x=hex
  -e, --encoding=ENCODING  select character encoding:
                             s=7-bit-ascii (default), S=8-bit-UTF8,
                             b=16-bit-big-endian, l=16-bit-little-endian,
                             B=32-bit-big-endian, L=32-bit-little-endian
  -o                       print offset before each string (alias for -t o)

Exit status:
  0  if any string was found
  1  if no string was found or error occurred

messages.command.stty.description:
Print or change terminal characteristics.

With no arguments, prints all terminal settings in human-readable form.

Mandatory arguments to long options are mandatory for short options too.

  -a, --all     print all current settings in human-readable form
  -g, --save    print all current settings in a stty-readable form
  -F, --file    open and use the specified device instead of stdin

Settings:
  sane          reset all settings to reasonable defaults
  raw           disable all input processing
  cooked        enable standard input processing
  cbreak        like -icanon with min=1
  echo          echo input characters
  -echo         do not echo input characters
  icanon        enable canonical (line) mode
  -icanon       disable canonical mode
  isig          enable interrupt/quit signals
  -isig         disable interrupt/quit signals

Note: On Windows, only echo/icanon/isig settings have actual effect.
Other settings are accepted but silently ignored.

messages.command.stty.option.save: print all current settings in a stty-readable form

messages.command.top.description:
The top program provides a dynamic real-time view of a running system.
It can display system summary information as well as a list of processes
or threads currently being managed by the Linux kernel.

The types of system summary information shown and the types, order and
size of information displayed for processes are all user configurable
and that configuration can be made persistent across restarts.

The program provides a limited interactive interface for process
manipulation as well as a much more extensive interface for personal
configuration - encompassing every aspect of its operation. And while
top is referred to throughout this document, you are free to name the
program anything you wish. That new name, possibly an alias, will then
be reflected on top's display and used when reading and writing a
configuration file.

  \t    horizontal tab
  \v    vertical tab

messages.command.tree.description:
tree is a recursive directory listing program that produces a depth indented
listing of files. Color is supported ala dircolors if the LS_COLORS environment
variable is set, outputting to tty.

With no arguments, tree lists the files in the current directory. When directory
arguments are given, tree lists all the files and/or directories found in the
given directories each in turn. Upon completion of listing all files/directories
found, tree returns the total number of files and/or directories listed.

By default, when a symbolic link is encountered, the path that the symbolic link
refers to is printed after the name of the link in the format:
    name -> real-path

If the -f option is given, then each entry is printed with its full path prefix.

messages.command.tzset.custom_help:
Usage: tzset [OPTION]

Print POSIX-compatible timezone ID from current Windows timezone setting

Options:
      --help               output usage information and exit.
  -V, --version            output version information and exit.

Use tzset to set your TZ variable. In POSIX-compatible shells like bash,
dash, mksh, or zsh:

      export TZ=$(tzset)

In csh-compatible shells like tcsh:

      setenv TZ `tzset`

messages.command.wpm.custom_help:
Winux Package Manager {}
Usage: wpm <command> [args] [options]

Commands:
  links list|rebuild|remove             manage WinuxCmd hardlinks
  clean [cache|staging|all]             remove transient downloads and staging
  cache clean [cache|staging|all]       alias for clean
  index status|update                   inspect or refresh local index
  update-index                          alias for index update
  source list|use|add|test              manage and test index sources
  list                                  list indexed packages and install state
  categories                            list package categories and counts
  search <query>                        search names, commands, categories, licenses
  info <package>                        show package metadata
  install <package>...                  install one or more packages
  installed                             list packages present in this root
  export [--plain]                      print installed package names for profiles
  restore <file>                        install packages from a plain list
  outdated                              list installed packages with updates
  uninstall|remove|erase <package>...   uninstall one or more packages
  update|upgrade winuxcmd               update WinuxCmd from local index

Options:
  -r, --root <dir>                      manage a specific WinuxCmd root
  -s, --source <name>                   use a specific index source
  -a, --all                             show index-only packages in list output
  -f, --force                           overwrite existing files when safe
  -n, --dry-run                         show planned changes without writing
  -v, --verbose                         print detailed progress
  -y, --yes                             assume yes for interactive prompts
      --category <name>                 filter list/search output by category
      --json                            print machine-readable JSON
      --plain                           print only package names for export
      --help                            display this help and exit
  -V, --version                         output version information and exit
